Monica Seles stands on the podium at Roland Garros, clutching the silver Coupe Suzanne Lenglen trophy. Dressed in a white FILA tracksuit with purple accents, she beams upward, her blue eyes reflecting pride and relief after securing her first French Open title in 1990.

Seles’s victory at age 16 marked the beginning of a remarkable Grand Slam career. By 1993, she had dominated the women’s tour, winning seven of nine majors and holding the world No. 1 ranking. However, her ascent was tragically interrupted when she was stabbed during a match in Hamburg, Germany, sidelining her for over two years.

Despite the attack’s physical and psychological toll, Seles returned to win the 1996 Australian Open and continued competing until 2003. This image of her lifting the Coupe Suzanne Lenglen remains a testament to her early brilliance on the clay courts of Paris.
